intro: One rule decides where code lives: anything a browser or a person touches is JavaScript; anything that needs the scientific Python stack (numpy, OpenCV, PyTorch) or touches models is Python. The two meet at one narrow, authenticated HTTP seam, and the website works when the seam is closed.

rows.why: The whole site is a handful of files and a route table. Making a visitor's page depend on a second process would only add a way for it to fail.
They must run first, on every request, in the one process that faces the browser. The model service repeats the ones that matter (Host, key, JSON only) because it must be safe on its own.

rows.piece: .env to settings, and what the browser may see
rows.why: One place decides the public summary, so no secret can leak by accident. Python needs the same file, so it has a second reader, and tests/fixtures/env-cases.json runs against both so they cannot drift.
Signing in and retrying an HTTP call needs no scientific library, and it keeps the basic Design Studio working without Python installed.

rows.piece: Starting and supervising the model service
rows.why: Whoever serves the website decides what to do when a helper dies. The website never waits for it and never throws because of it.

rows.piece: Site build, link check, this overview
rows.why: Text processing on files, in the same runtime as the server, so a clone needs Node and nothing else to build and check the site.
It decodes photos, rotates them, builds masks from polygons and feeds the rest of the pipeline: Pillow and numpy territory. It has its own small Google client so the service runs on its own.
PyTorch and transformers exist only here. The backends (local SAM 2, SAM 3 on a GPU, a remote server) are all models.
Dense array work with OpenCV and numpy (dynamic programming along every boundary). The evaluation tools call the same functions, so the measured numbers are the shipped code's numbers.
Datasets, training loops and metrics. They need to import the pipeline directly, not call it over HTTP.

seam.title: The seam
points: Express listens on PORT. The model service listens on 127.0.0.1 on a port the system chooses and prints it in one READY line.
Express streams /api/segment and /api/sam/* to it with a shared key in X-Terucon-Model-Key (random per run when Express starts it).
The service answers in JSON with the same error shape, so a failure reaches the person as a plain message.
Express never needs the service to answer /api/config or /api/health, and the Studio falls back to its in-browser parser when it does not.

finetuning.title: A tuned Gemini for detection
finetuning.text: Point SWATCHROOM_DETECT_MODEL at the tuned model or endpoint name. detect_surfaces sends it the same structured-output request. No code changes.

finetuning.title: Your own SAM weights
finetuning.text: Set SAM_MODEL_ID to a Hugging Face repository or a local folder written by save_pretrained. The backend decides between SAM 2 and the original SAM by looking for sam2 or sam-2 in that string, so a local SAM 2 fine-tune must live in a folder whose path contains sam2. Or use SAM_BACKEND=sam3 with SAM_CHECKPOINT and SAM_REPO_DIR. A new kind of backend is a class in backends.py next to HfSamBackend.

finetuning.title: A new stage in the pipeline
finetuning.text: sharpen() takes rough outlines and returns one label map: SAM correction, then snapping, then layering. A learned edge model or a mask refiner is one more step in it, switched by a setting.

finetuning.title: Measure before and after
finetuning.text: refine_eval.py runs the same sharpen() the service runs against ground-truth photos and reports overlap and boundary accuracy, so a tuned model is compared on the shipped code path.

finetuning.title: Train and serve in one place
finetuning.text: model/finetune/ holds training scripts, data recipes and the notes of a run, once they exist. They import terucon_model for the label vocabulary and geometry, so training and serving cannot disagree about what a surface is. Build new photo sets for each round: the sets used so far are spent.

finetuning.title: Run it where the GPU is
finetuning.text: Start the service on the GPU machine with npm run model (MODEL_HOST, MODEL_PORT, MODEL_SERVICE_KEY) and point this website at it with MODEL_SERVICE=external and MODEL_SERVICE_URL.

finetuning_intro: Everything about the models lives in model/, so fine-tuning has one home. There is no training code yet; what exists is the evaluation that says whether a tuned model helps, and these places a tuned model plugs in, from least to most code.
